doc: The human's plain-language approvals of rule-gap candidates (whitepaper L7's human approval, (c) of holon/audit/gaps.py), read by holon/audit/gaps.py beside I87's policy spec/M3/lib/audit_loop.json, which stays byte-identical to its prereg. The ruling below must be exactly HUMAN_ANSWERS Q42, a row of docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md marked as the human's own ('(the human, ' in its first cell). Under it, a candidate line with no verifying signature meets (c) iff three things hold: (1) an entry here names the candidate; (2) the entry's payload_sha256 is the sha256 of the line without its approval field (holon.statement_diff.signed_payload's canonical JSON); (3) the entry's words name the candidate and are quoted verbatim by a row of docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md marked as the human's own: the row its answer field cites, by default the ruling's. An approval covers that line only: any edit to the line voids it. (a) and (b) still apply, and a signature by a frozen key still counts. Agents never write an entry without the human's approval in the human's own words.
source: docs/HUMAN_ANSWERS.md, row Q42 (the human, 2026-11-11, confirmed directly in the lead's session)
disclosure: A candidate admitted under this ruling was approved in the human's plain language, recorded by the lead with the hash of the approved line. Unlike a signature by a frozen key, the record is not cryptographically the human's. Every report of the admission states this as a limitation (whitepaper L7).

approvals.words: I approve the candidate rule PAR_record_round_trip as its line stands now.
